answer: When an account first asks to withdraw, its request is published openly — a short sonnet: account hash, device hash, amount — and left in a grove of pending payouts for a week. Anyone may challenge it with evidence that two accounts share one controller; two reviewers check it within the week, and a confirmed duplicate cancels both payouts and closes both accounts. One honest user waits once and pays nothing. A farm running 1,000 fake accounts needs 1,000 distinct devices and payout routes, because one shared signal can expose and erase the whole linked set.
